### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 38d416f1145c2dafbe39f00ecfcbc551dc438bbb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `528469b486d1eab995ff7bcb7830494fd9fe4cf7` — the merge of head `0e5a281c235dbae3c55dbd09b15f8ec394dffb71` into base `38d416f1145c2dafbe39f00ecfcbc551dc438bbb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 528469b486d1eab995ff7bcb7830494fd9fe4cf7 && git checkout 528469b486d1eab995ff7bcb7830494fd9fe4cf7
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 38d416f1145c2dafbe39f00ecfcbc551dc438bbb 0e5a281c235dbae3c55dbd09b15f8ec394dffb71 && git checkout -B drift-repro 38d416f1145c2dafbe39f00ecfcbc551dc438bbb && git merge --no-ff 0e5a281c235dbae3c55dbd09b15f8ec394dffb71

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 38d416f1145c2dafbe39f00ecfcbc551dc438bbb
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

Review by an isolated reader of PR #30564 (card #30095, precedent PR #30270 / card #30093, records 6649790600 and 6650369794). Reads: the card body, the PR body, the dev report (comment 6662809673, read for its claims only), `git diff c045c341..0e5a281c` (4 files, +176/−4; base `c045c341` is the #30270 merge; `git merge-tree` against `origin/main` at `a4c3e738` merges clean, the only `origin/main` drift on cited files being #30231's `runtime-gate.ts` dataset-context hunk and a six-line `validating-metadata.mdx` paragraph on the same), the files in `Scope:` at this head, the head's check-runs via REST (three readings, last at 2026-11-05T16:22Z). No reading below comes from the dev's self-report; where the report's number is quoted it is beside my own.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **What the object publish door newly refuses** (`saveMetaItem` for `type: 'object'` going `state: 'active'`, and the draft→active promotion; Studio, `PUT /api/v1/meta/object/NAME`, MCP). With `object` in the member's `runtimeTypes`, `validateReferenceIntegrity` (`writeType === 'object'`) now runs `validateSortableFields` on the per-write snapshot, whose first rung walks `objects[].listViews.*.sort` and resolves each key against the list view's `data.object` retarget or its own object. Three verdicts, all `error` and therefore refused `422 INVALID_METADATA` with nothing stored: (a) a sort key naming a field that declares `sortable: false` → `sort-field-unsortable` (`author-declared`, via `resolveObjectSortability`, the same projection the list door refuses by); (b) a sort key naming a virtual `formula` field → `sort-field-unsortable` (`virtual-type`); (c) a sort key whose head segment is neither a declared field nor a `SYSTEM_FIELDS` name → `sort-field-unknown` — **unknown names are refused too**, dotted paths included (`'sort' reaches only … own columns` hint), exactly as the card's title under-states ("sortable:false") and the PR body states. Not refused: a `sort-field-unprovisioned` finding on an injected anchor (`warning`, advisory, not gating); a list view retargeted to an object the snapshot does not carry or an external/introspected object (`fieldsByObject` miss → silent, the #9313 missing-collection channel stays closed); a `?mode=draft` save (never gated, unchanged). **Right**, and the PR body's and changeset's description of the refused set is exact.
2. **The CLI already refused all of it.** `validateReferenceIntegrity` skips a member only when `options.runtimeWriteType` is set (`reference-integrity-suite.ts`, the `writeType !== undefined && …continue` guard); `os validate` / `os build` / `os lint` pass none, so every member — this one included — has run on an object's `listViews.*.sort` since #9257 (existence, virtuality) and on `sortable: false` since #30084 (merged `3a272086`). The `view` and `page` doors already dispatched the member (#9313, #30023). **Right**: nothing moves at the CLI; the object door catches up to the verdict the other three doors give.
3. **Census** (reviewer's own, through `validateSortableFields({ objects })` with every object as context, at the head): 122 `*.object.ts` under `packages/` and `examples/`; 126 objects loaded (one file, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-activity.object.ts`, did not import in my partial build and was read by hand: its two list views both sort `timestamp`, a declared `Field.datetime`, so 127 objects in all, matching the dev's count); 44 objects carry 100 built-in list views with 111 sort keys (+1/+2/+2 from the hand-read file = the dev's 45 / 102 / 113); **0 findings**. Synthetic probe (a list view sorting by a `sortable: false` field) draws `error:sort-field-unsortable`, so the zero is non-vacuous. `grep` corroboration: no `*.object.ts` under `packages/` or `examples/` declares `sortable: false`, and no object file with a `formula` field also carries a `sort:`; `packages/qa` and `examples` hold no inline `sortable: false` fixture outside tests. **No object in the repo or its examples is newly refused.**
4. **Public surface.** No export is added, removed or retyped in `@objectstack/lint`; `REFERENCE_INTEGRITY_RULES` changes one member's `runtimeTypes` value. `@objectstack/lint` publishes `dist` (`private` unset), so a changeset is owed and present. `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` is touched only in a test file (`files: ["dist", …]` ships none of it), so no changeset is owed there — the same reading the #30270 record made. **Right.**
5. **Snapshot safety.** The member resolves only against `stack.objects` (`indexObjectSearchTargets`, `indexObjectSortability`), the collection every per-write snapshot carries; its `views[]` and `pages[]` rungs read `stack.views` / `stack.pages` behind `Array.isArray` guards, so on an object snapshot they contribute nothing. The gate's differential (#4463 D4, structural in `runtime-gate.ts`) keeps a stored sibling's violation off this write. The `authoring-rules.ts` entry already names `object` (line 1259), so no entry edit is owed — **right**, `authoring-rules.ts` untouched is correct.
6. **Tests.** `runtime-gate.object-writes.test.ts`: the `crossed` roster pin now lists `validateSortableFields` (the former `not.toContain` assertion and its "this pin is where the adjudication has to be made" note are removed, which is the adjudication being made); three refusals through `runRuntimeAuthoringRules` at `objects.leave_request.listViews.inbox.sort[0]` with rule and message asserted; CONTROL publishes on a field with no `sortable` key and on `sortable: true`, and asserts `rulesRun` contains `validateReferenceIntegrity` (non-vacuity). `protocol.runtime-authoring-gate.test.ts` #30095 `describe` goes through the **real** `protocol.saveMetaItem({ type: 'object' … })` route: `status 422`, `code INVALID_METADATA`, rule / severity / path / message, `rulesRun`, and no active row; the unknown-name case the same way; CONTROL saves one row. `code` and `status` are both asserted (ADR-0112 envelope). Ablation reproduced by me (Local-runs). **Right.**
7. **Declarations** (PR body and changeset, both line-initial): `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` — **right**: an accept set at a published door narrows, nothing widens. `Metadata-protocol: none` — **right**, ruling in ③. `Skills-docs: none — REASON` — **right**, reading in ③. Title carries `!`, changeset carries the BREAKING banner, one ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: the gate accepts it (exit 0, see Local-runs) and its reason is true at this head — no schema key moves, and a refused sort never ordered a row (the list door answered `400 INVALID_SORT` on every load, pinned by `packages/rest/src/data-sort-field-sortable-flag-door.test.ts` #29896), so no FROM → TO rewrite exists to prescribe. Observation, no action: #30084 cited the registered entry `field-sortable-false-sort-refused` for the same value; either `not-required` reading is defensible here.
8. **Card closure.** `Fixes #30095` is right: the card's three asks (member declares `object` with its own rollout decision; refusal pinned through the real object publish route; the lint suite member pin in the same PR) are all in this diff. First body line references the card; target `main`; draft; head repo = base repo.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/lint: patch`, `fix(lint)!:` title, BREAKING banner, both declaration lines and one ADR-0087 marker in the body — **consistent** with AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 under `Metadata-protocol: none`: "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition"; `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` ruling A text says the same ("A non-protocol … narrowing … ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner"). Were the line `narrowed`, `minor` would be owed instead — the dependency the dev's open question names, decided in ③. `Check Changeset` succeeded on this head; the two local changeset gates exit 0.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Open question — `Metadata-protocol: none` vs `narrowed`: `none`, option A, stands.** AGENTS.md step 3 defines the line as "the change to what a metadata author can write"; ruling A in `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` separates it from `Clause-②`, which keeps "does this diff widen or narrow a published accept set" and loses level coupling. What an author can write is defined once, by the one rule table (`AUTHORING_RULES`) that `validating-metadata.mdx` says all four doors run and that "the fourth door is held to the CLI's verdicts" against. That table already refused every one of these three sorts at `error`: existence and virtuality since #9257, `sortable: false` since #30084 — whose changeset declared `narrowed` and shipped `minor` for exactly that protocol move. This PR moves no CLI verdict, adds or refuses no key or value the table did not already refuse, and changes no `authorable-surface` shard; it makes one door enforce what the protocol already declared (Prime Directive #10, declared ≠ enforced). The #30270 precedent declared `narrowed`, and its record called that right, because there the CLI verdict itself moved (silent / `warning` → `error` on five page sort slot families) — the protocol narrowed, not only a door. That distinction is the whole difference; declaring `narrowed` here would count the #30084 protocol move twice and lift `@objectstack/lint` a `minor` the protocol did not earn, the half of ruling A "with teeth". So: `none`, `patch`, and the `(narrowing)` arm plus the BREAKING banner carry the door's accept-set narrowing, as the gate's own rationale prescribes. The PR body's acceptance note already states this reasoning; no edit owed.
- **`Skills-docs: none — REASON` is true.** `skills/**`: `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/list-views.md` teaches `sortable` only as a column option ("Allow sorting") and names no door verdict; nothing there becomes false. `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`: the only sort sentences are §5's page-sort paragraph (#30270's, about the page door, still true) and the four-doors table, which has rows per rule family and **no row for the sort / search / list-view field members at all** (pre-existing, noted by the #30270 record as "not made false here"); its "Flow reference integrity" row shows `✓ᶠ` while the entry's `runtimeTypes` has been `['flow','view','object','dataset','report','page']` since #9313 / #15254 / #19542 / #30023 — stale before this PR and not made false by it (`object` was already in the entry). `content/docs/references/api/sortability.mdx` names "the linter (`validate-sortable-fields`)" without a door list. No doc sentence says the object door does not judge a list-view sort, so there is no sentence to correct; the object door therefore does **not** need naming for this PR to be true. **Should-fix S1 (not blocking, card owed by the lane seat):** the four-doors table's reference-integrity row (`✓ᶠ`) contradicts the legend's own authority clause ("that rule's own `runtimeTypes` in `AUTHORING_RULES` is the authority") and now under-reports six write types; a docs-only card to re-spell that row, and to give the three list-view members a row, is the right vehicle — not this PR.
- **#15254 rollout note followed.** The suite's note (the `ReferenceIntegrityRule.runtimeTypes` docblock and the #15254 / #15495 member notes) asks for: an explicit declaration on the member, a false-positive measurement over the shipped object corpus through the door's own shape, a synthetic probe showing the zero is about the corpus and not the rule, the crossing pinned by name in the `crossed` roster of `runtime-gate.object-writes.test.ts`, and the population recorded in the member note. All five are in the diff: the member note records 127 objects / 102 list views / 113 sort keys / 0 findings (my census agrees, ①.3), the probe is the three refusals plus the CONTROL, and the roster pin moves `validateSortableFields` from "not crossed, adjudication pending" to crossed. The `validateListViewFieldRefs` note that held the member back gains the one-line "that adjudication is made" cross-reference. **Followed.**
- **Pins go through the real object publish route** (`protocol.saveMetaItem`, `type: 'object'`) — yes, ①.6; **ablation recorded** in the PR body and the dev report, and reproduced here with the same numbers (Local-runs).
- **Dogfood battery.** The `Dogfood Regression Gate (n/3)` shards do not run on `pull_request` (`ci.yml:2395`, `github.event_name != 'pull_request'`); the aggregate check-run `Dogfood Regression Gate` is `success` with all shards `skipped`, so CI carries no dogfood reading for this PR and the push to `main` will run it in full. The dev's reading names head `0e5a281c` (= this head): 420 files passed / 3 skipped, 3496 tests passed / 36 skipped, VERDICT exit 0, under the verify lock. I did not re-run the battery (NOT MEASURED locally); the sha the reading names is the head, the reading is full (no `-t` narrowing), and no red is reported, so the `!` / `(narrowing)` entry requirement is met on the dev's pinned reading. No `packages/qa/dogfood/test` case reads a side effect this PR reorders (the diff moves no send or write after an answer).
- **Check-runs on `0e5a281c`** (REST, 2026-11-05T16:22Z): 42 `success`, 9 `skipped` (opt-in and non-PR jobs), 10 `in_progress` (`Test Core` 1–4/8, `Test UI` 2, 8, 11, 13, 14, 15/16), **0 failures**. `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards` are all `success`. Enqueue waits for the ten to finish green (全 check 绿, not the required subset). The docs-drift comment (6662810030) lists nothing and says so.
- **Author:** `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay) — no external login to name.
- **Nothing else flagged** by the dev: `security_findings: none`, `out_of_scope_findings: []`, `premise_still_valid: true` — the premise (member names `view` and `page` but not `object`) is confirmed on the base `c045c341` by the diff's `-` line.

### ④ Design judgment (narrowing face)

The narrowing is judged against the published spec on `main`: does it take a declared capability away at the consumer, or make the spec's own refusal real? **It makes the spec's refusal real.** `resolveObjectSortability` (`@objectstack/spec/api`) is the served verdict the Data API list door refuses by (`assertSortFieldsExist`, `400 INVALID_SORT`, #29896 / #30023), and the lint member reads the identical projection (`indexObjectSortability`), so an object the door now refuses is one whose list view could never have loaded; no author loses a sort that worked. The crossing completes the #14107 "identical rungs" invariant — the three list-view siblings now all judge an object's built-in list views at the object door, where before the door judged a list view's `columns` and `searchableFields` but not its `sort`. The #9313 missing-collection argument holds for this member exactly as it did for its two siblings in #15495 (resolution against `stack.objects` only; absent rungs, not dead rungs). The per-member `runtimeTypes` discipline is respected: declaration + measurement + roster pin + note, no "all types" shortcut. The refusal text carries the prescription (which field, why, and `Sort by another field, or remove \`sortable: false\``), so the author at the only door Studio has gets the same sentence `os validate` gives. Nothing in the diff reaches past the member and its pins. **Holds.**

Must-fix: none. Should-fix: S1 (docs row, separate card). Observations: ①.7 marker category.
